neighbours.label: a noun-like word used as a verb (to air, to surface, to clinch, unearth), not the same word as a noun
fire: The final episode will air on public television next Friday.
Fresh allegations may surface once the documents are released.
A draw tonight would be enough for the club to clinch promotion.
Workers digging the foundation could unearth Roman coins.
The interview is set to air after the evening news.
Problems like these tend to surface only after a few years of use.
The radio station agreed to air the debate in full.
They hope to clinch the deal before the end of the quarter.
quiet: The final episode was filmed in a room with no fresh air.
The ice on the surface of the lake was thin.
A draw tonight would leave the club in second place.
Workers found the foundation full of Roman coins.
The air outside smelled of smoke after the fire.
Cracks appeared on the surface after a few years of use.
The radio station has a small studio in the basement.
They signed the deal before the end of the quarter.

predictions: Fire on air/surface/clinch/unearth when they are verbs after 'to', 'could', 'will'; quiet when the same words are nouns or adjectives.
